name: Lemongrass (West Indian)
source_reference: ISO 3217:1974 - Oil of lemongrass; Arctander, 'Perfume and Flavor Materials of Natural Origin', 1960; Schaneberg & Khan, J. Agric. Food Chem., 2002
notes: C. citratus (West Indian) and C. flexuosus (East Indian) are both traded as lemongrass oil. East Indian has higher citral content (up to 85%) and more aldehydic sharpness. West Indian is generally preferred in fragrance for its fuller body.

key_markers.141-27-5: Geranial - dominant lemon-aldehyde, the sharper isomer of citral
key_markers.106-26-3: Neral - softer, sweeter isomer of citral; ratio to geranial is diagnostic
key_markers.123-35-3: Myrcene - fresh, green terpene providing body and natural character

olfactive_description: Strong, fresh, lemon-aldehyde character with a grassy-green herbaceous body. More pungent and less refined than lemon, with a distinctive hay-like dry undertone. Powerful and diffusive.
